extracted.intended_audience: early-career tenure-track assistant professors in biomedical sciences and chemistry; university research administrators and research offices
extracted.subtask_description: Program description and selection criteria for the Searle Scholars Program, which awards $300,000 over three years to support independent research of exceptional, recently appointed tenure‑track assistant professors in chemistry and the biomedical sciences. Explains who may be nominated, what kinds of research are favored, award terms, and who selects the Scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment status / eligibility (assistant professor, tenure-track)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports the independent research of exceptional young faculty in the biomedical sciences and chemistry who have recently been appointed as assistant professors on a tenure-track appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to be early-career faculty recently appointed to tenure-track assistant professor positions; the program makes grants to selected universities and research centers to support these individuals. (Original phrasing: 'recently been appointed as assistant professors on a tenure-track appointment.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Research independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The award supports the independent research of the Scholar — flexible funding to support their own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are made to institutions to enable the Scholar to pursue an independent research program. The program emphasizes supporting the Scholar's own work rather than collaborative pilot funding directed by senior PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary scope (chemistry and biomedical sciences; broad range)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program funds research in chemistry and the biomedical sciences and describes support for 'a broad range of scientific disciplines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of supported topics given include blood–brain barrier delivery, fungal manipulation of neural systems, glycan-mediated immune evasion, reconstitution of signaling pathways, and many others — indicating broad topical latitude within the biomedical/chemical sphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: High risk / high reward emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program supports high risk, high reward research across a broad range of scientific disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program favors projects that are potentially transformative and exploratory; flexible funding ($300,000 over three years) is provided to enable ambitious, possibly higher-risk lines of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and commitment to an academic research career
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars are chosen based on rigorous standards aimed at finding 'the most creative talent interested in pursuing an academic research career.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors creative investigators who demonstrate an intention to continue in academia and lead independent research programs. The Scientific Advisory Board explicitly seeks candidates with these qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise of field-changing impact and translational potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection recognizes candidates for their 'promise to change their fields' and to 'develop next-generation technologies that can reveal biological function.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for evidence that the proposed work could substantially advance fundamental understanding or reveal strategies relevant to therapeutics; examples in the announcement illustrate such ambitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Milan Mrksich, the program’s Scientific Director, appoints a Scientific Advisory Board of eminent scientists who choose the Scholars based on rigorous standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is governed by an appointed Scientific Advisory Board rather than an open public vote; decisions are made by peer experts chosen by the program director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination/application mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are considered from nominations by universities and research institutions (this year 194 applications from nominations by 145 universities and research institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective candidates are nominated by their institutions; institutional nomination appears to be a required step in the application pipeline rather than direct self-application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount, term, and payment structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are $300,000 for a three-year term, with $100,000 payable each year of the grant. Funding is flexible to support the Scholar's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are administered to the host institution and are intended as flexible support for the Scholar over a three-year period. (Original phrasing: 'Grants are $300,000 for a three-year term, with $100,000 payable each year of the grant.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and funding source
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program is funded through the Searle Funds at The Chicago Community Trust and administered by Kinship Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative and funding arrangements are specified — applicants and host institutions should route award management through the listed entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record / prestige indicators (implicit selection signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program highlights past outcomes: since 1981, 707 scientists named; program awarded more than $161 million; many past Scholars have achieved NAS membership, MacArthur Fellowships, and Nobel Prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a formal selection criterion, the program emphasizes that successful Scholars tend to be those with the potential for exceptional long-term impact; applicants may infer that evidence of exceptional promise and future impact strengthens candidacy.
